description: The Gaza Ministry of Health counted 310 health workers detained as of June 2024. Healthcare Workers Watch reported that by July 2025 over 400 Palestinian healthcare workers, including at least 28 doctors, had been detained since October 2023 - many held over 400 days without charge, and three for over 600 days.
energy_note: Four hundred days in custody, no charge, for being a nurse.

aspect: The proportion of one facility's population
description: Dr Khalid Hamouda, himself a detainee, estimated about a quarter of the roughly 100 detainees held at Sde Teiman were healthcare workers.
energy_note: One in four of the room, medical staff.

description: Physicians for Human Rights Israel published 'Unlawfully Detained, Tortured, and Starved: The Plight of Gaza's Medical Workers in Israeli Custody' in February 2025, based on testimony from 24 detainees - physicians, nurses and paramedics aged from at least 21 to 69 - visited by PHRI lawyers in military and prison service facilities after more than six months in isolation. It documented beatings, torture, psychological abuse, medical neglect and insufficient rations.

aspect: EXAMPLE - specific methods, from the testimony
description: One detainee described being suspended by her wrists for hours. Others described being severely beaten under interrogation and subjected to prolonged high-volume music. Healthcare Workers Watch-Palestine collected 31 accounts describing stress positions, food and water deprivation, threats of sexual violence and degrading treatment.
energy_note: Suspended by the wrists, for hours.

aspect: The interrogations were about the hospital, not the person
description: Detainees were not charged or individually accused; interrogations focused on collecting information about their workplace, their colleagues and Gaza's health system. PHRI's Naji Abbas described this as aimed at finding information useful to the assault, and as a violation of Geneva Convention protections for medical workers.
energy_note: Held not for what you did, but for what you know about your ward.

aspect: EXAMPLE - hospital directors taken with their staff
description: OHCHR gathered credible information that raids on hospitals often led to mass detention and enforced disappearance of medical staff, including the directors of Al Awda, Kamal Adwan, Al Shifa and Al Amal. Dr Muhammad Abu Salmiya, Al-Shifa's director, was held without charge for seven months until July 2024. Kamal Adwan's director Hussam Abu Safiya was detained along with more than 240 Palestinians including dozens of medical staff.
energy_note: The director, and two hundred and forty others.

description: HRW documented the same pattern in August 2024, as did B'Tselem in August 2024 and Healthcare Workers Watch. The IDF and Prison Service denied the allegations.
energy_note: Four bodies, the same finding, and a denial.

aspect: Removing the medical workforce is a harm to everyone else
description: Every detained surgeon is a queue that does not move, and every detained midwife is a birth without one. The harm to the population is separate from, and larger than, the harm to the detainee.
energy_note: The doctor is in prison, so the ward has no one.
